briefs.label: Zoom in
briefs.brief: a magnifying glass with a bold plus sign inside the lens, zoom in
briefs.meaning: Zooms the map in a step.
briefs.reference: Set One, final round, top row 2nd

briefs.label: Zoom out
briefs.brief: the same magnifying glass with a bold minus sign inside the lens, zoom out
briefs.meaning: Zooms the map out a step.
briefs.reference: Set One, final round, top row 2nd

briefs.label: Fit
briefs.brief: four thick corner brackets around a compact cluster of seven large olive hexagons, fit to view
briefs.meaning: Fits the whole map in the pane. At most seven hexes, or it turns to mush at 16 px.
briefs.reference: Set One, final round, top row 2nd

briefs.label: Rotate map
briefs.brief: the same cluster of seven large olive hexagons, one hexagon brick red, with a single thick curved arrow sweeping a quarter turn around it, rotate
briefs.meaning: Turns the whole map a quarter clockwise. One arrow, never two: two read as refresh.
briefs.reference: Set One, final round, top row 2nd

briefs.label: Selection
briefs.brief: a single large olive hexagon with a classic slate-navy mouse pointer arrow touching its lower right edge, selection
briefs.meaning: The hex or counter last clicked, and its facts.
briefs.reference: Set Two, final round, top row 3rd

briefs.label: LOS
briefs.brief: a small bold eye in the upper left corner, a thick dashed sight line starting at the outer corner of the eye and running diagonally down to one small olive hexagon in the lower right corner, the line never crosses or overlaps the eye, line of sight
briefs.meaning: Line of sight in ASL is a straight line between hex centers: never bent. A line through the eye reads as hide.
briefs.reference: Set Two, final round, bottom row 3rd

briefs.label: Range
briefs.brief: a straight horizontal row of four hexagons touching edge to edge, only the two end hexagons solid olive, the two middle hexagons outlined only, a slate-navy bracket under the whole row, range counted in hexes
briefs.meaning: Range is counted in hexes, not measured with a ruler.
briefs.reference: Set Two, final round, top row 3rd

briefs.label: Unit Planner
briefs.brief: a cream clipboard with a bold slate-navy outline and a solid slate-navy clip at the top, three short horizontal bars on the sheet, one small olive hexagon with a brick red dot overlapping the lower right corner, unit planner
briefs.meaning: The tab that holds LOS, Range, and the Movement Plan: the player's plans for his units, not a game action.
briefs.reference: Drawn in the Studio, 2026-10-21 (the Play streamlining plan, S8); no Midjourney set yet

briefs.label: Movement Plan
briefs.brief: one small solid olive hexagon in the lower left corner, a thick dashed slate-navy line running diagonally up through one outlined hexagon in the middle to a brick red arrowhead in the upper right corner, a planned route
briefs.meaning: A route for each stack, made one stack after another (A4.2): the hexes it will enter, not a straight line of sight.
briefs.reference: Drawn in the Studio, 2026-10-21 (the Play streamlining plan, S8); no Midjourney set yet

briefs.label: Evidence
briefs.brief: an open book with cream pages and a bold slate-navy outline, three thick horizontal bars on each page, one brick red bookmark ribbon hanging from the bottom center, evidence
briefs.meaning: The rule citations and grid samples behind what the inspector shows. Horizontal bars: vertical ones read as a barcode.
briefs.reference: Set Two, final round, top row 3rd

briefs.label: Layers
briefs.brief: three flat-topped hexagons seen at a slant, stacked one above another like sheets, cream on top, olive in the middle, sage at the bottom, each with a bold slate-navy outline, map layers
briefs.meaning: The board viewer's rendered layers and the counter style. Hexes, as the boards' own, rather than the usual squares.
briefs.reference: Drawn by make_icons.py to match its neighbors (2026-10-18), not from Midjourney

briefs.label: Proposal
briefs.brief: a clipboard with a checkmark box and a pencil, a proposed order awaiting confirmation
briefs.meaning: An order proposed but not yet carried out: the side reviews it, then confirms or cancels. Not a finished order, so not a bare checkmark.

briefs.label: Play
briefs.brief: a square game counter with an off-white face and a thick olive frame with rounded corners, bearing a bold slate-navy silhouette of a WWII infantryman in a steel helmet advancing mid-stride with his rifle at the ready, his helmet brim, face, pack, arms, rifle, belt, and legs delineated by subtle thin white piping lines inside the silhouette, play the game
briefs.meaning: Where the side plays: its actions in the game. A squad counter with its soldier figure, as ASL is played; never a media play triangle. The silhouette stays one bold shape: the piping is subtle hairlines, never gaps, and the face is off-white so the white piping reads. At 20 px only the counter and the figure survive.
briefs.reference: Play, with piping (2026-10-17-5): the user's pick, traced

briefs.label: Records
briefs.brief: a stack of three ruled record sheets with a pair of dice resting on the bottom corner, the game records
briefs.meaning: Every roll and every action recorded so far, latest first; each record opens its step on Replay. Sheets and dice, not a book: Evidence already has the book.
briefs.reference: Inspector tabs, second set (2026-10-17-6): the user's pick, top left

briefs.label: Units
briefs.brief: a stack of three square game counters, each slightly offset up and to the right, the top one bearing a small slate-navy soldier silhouette, the units in play
briefs.meaning: The units the view may see, in a table. A stack of counters, as ASL stacks units in a hex; the plural of the Play counter, so it must not look like a single counter.
briefs.reference: Inspector tabs, second set (2026-10-17-6): the user's pick, top right

briefs.label: Scripted dice
briefs.brief: a white die and a brick red die side by side, beside a small ruled list sheet, scripted dice for tests
briefs.meaning: Test runs only: dice queued in advance. ASL rolls a white die and a coloured die, so one of the two is red.
briefs.reference: Inspector tabs, second set (2026-10-17-6): the user's pick, bottom left

briefs.label: Standing
briefs.brief: a small olive pennant flag on a slate-navy pole planted on a single hexagon, victory standing
briefs.meaning: How the Victory Conditions stand after the step shown: who holds what. A flag planted on a hex is control, not a trophy or a chart.
briefs.reference: Inspector tabs, second set (2026-10-17-6): the user's pick, bottom right

briefs.label: Step
briefs.brief: a short horizontal track of four square record boxes, an olive game counter sitting in the third box, a small brick red pointer above it, the step shown in the game's sequence
briefs.meaning: The one moment of the game the replay is on: its account, when it was, what changed, its dice. A marker on a turn record track, as on an ASL card; never media playback, a row of hexes (Range), sheets or dice (Records), or a footprint (movement).
